about.title: About
about.heading: About Logia
about.dek: A free, open library of Christian commentary, set verse by verse beside Scripture.
body: Logia sets each verse of the Bible beside what the church has said about it, from the early church to the 1800s. It is free to read, free to share, and its data is open for anyone to build on, in the spirit of Sefaria's library of Jewish texts.
The name comes from *ta logia tou theou*, “the oracles of God” (Romans 3:2), and from Papias's lost *Exposition of the Logia of the Lord*, one of the first Christian commentaries.

Every excerpt is copied from a public-domain edition, never rewritten, and the source text it came from is kept beside it. A script checks each excerpt against its source on every change: word for word for a transcription, and in runs of six words for a page scan, whose lines carry margin notes and running heads. Where a scan misread a letter (“Let ns” for “Let us”), the correction is listed openly and applied when the site is built.

Logia reads the Open Word Bible, a CC0 translation from Hebrew and Greek with the reasoning behind every sentence. Logia never edits it: it is imported at a pinned version from the Open Word Bible's own repository.

Logia starts in English. Each new language is translated from the best public-domain source, the original Greek, Latin or German where that is better than the English, and reviewed by native speakers before it is marked reviewed.
Logia's data and writing are CC0, its code is MIT, and everything is on GitHub.

linker.title: Link Bible references to Logia
linker.heading: Link Bible references to Logia
linker.dek: One line on your site turns every Bible reference into a link to that verse on Logia, with a preview of the verse and of who has commented on it.
linker.how_text: Put this line in your page, before </body> or in the <head>. It finds references such as John 3:16, Jn 1:14, 1 Cor. 13:4–7 or Rom 8:28 in the page's text and links them.
linker.options: Options, as attributes on the script tag:
linker.scope: only look inside the elements this CSS selector matches
linker.preview_off: make links, but show no preview cards
linker.skip: on any element, leaves its text alone (links, code and form fields are always left alone)
linker.example: In the beginning was the Word (John 1:1), and the Word became flesh (Jn 1:14). Love is patient and kind (1 Cor. 13:4–7). The heavens declare the glory of God (Ps 19:1), and the sun of righteousness shall rise (Mal 4:2). We know that all things work together for good (Rom 8:28). Is 53:5 is linked; “the train is 9:30” is not.
linker.data_text: The previews read Logia's public, read-only API ({api}), which any site or program may use: every verse's text and commentary, works, versions, authors and topics, as JSON. Its shape is documented in {docs}. Logia's data is CC0; the script is MIT.

rules.title: Editorial rules
rules.heading: How texts get into Logia
rules.dek: The rules every text in Logia follows, and the rights each one is used under, so anyone can check them.
rules: Every excerpt is copied from a public-domain edition exactly as it reads, and the source it came from is kept beside it. Nothing is paraphrased, summarised, modernised or filled in from memory. A script checks every excerpt against its source on every change.

Text and translation must be published in 1930 or earlier, which makes them public domain in the United States. Each version records its edition, translator and year, and what is still to confirm for use worldwide (the death dates of everyone named). Logia copies from scans and open transcriptions, not from sites that claim rights in their typed editions.
Greek and Hebrew are never retyped
Original-language words appear only as the source prints them. Where a scan turns Greek into noise, the Greek is left out and the cut is marked, rather than typed in by hand.
Scan misreadings are corrected in the open

An excerpt keeps the scan's text. A misreading is fixed by a listed correction (“Let ns” → “Let us”), applied when the site is built, and shown under the excerpt. Only what the printed page plainly says is fixed.
Places, citations and links are read from the sources
Where an excerpt sits in its work, the Scripture it cites and the Fathers a catena quotes are found by scripts from the sources, not typed. Each stays marked as unchecked until a person checks it.
Nothing is marked reviewed by an AI
Excerpts, versions, biographies, topics and translations are drafts until a named person reviews them, and the site says so.
The Bible text is imported, never edited
Logia reads the Open Word Bible at a pinned version. A problem with its wording is raised with the Open Word Bible, not changed here.
Every tradition, in its own words

Logia sets Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant voices side by side and takes no side where they differ. A commentator's words are kept whole, even when harsh or dated; a note may explain, but nothing is cut silently.
